long_biography.plain_text:
Thomas D. O’Malley reshaped independent refining by applying a commodity trader’s eye to neglected industrial assets. After rising from a trading-house mailroom to lead Salomon’s oil-trading division, he brought risk analysis and opportunistic purchasing to refinery ownership.

At Tosco, O’Malley bought plants that major oil companies regarded as peripheral, then combined lower acquisition costs with flexible crude sourcing, leased terminals and fuel retailing. The model turned a regional California refiner into a national operator and made him a prominent consolidator of the sector. Premcor supplied a further test of the strategy: acquisitions enlarged its refinery platform before the company was sold to a larger operator.

Premcor supplied a further test of the strategy: acquisitions enlarged its refinery platform before the company was sold to a larger operator.
